strings: Darkcore the Elder is a seasonal quest encountered during the Lunar Festival within the Undercity. By seeking out Elder Darkcore, travelers pay homage to the ancient spirits honored across Azeroth and receive a Coin of Ancestry in return.

During the Lunar Festival, spirits of ancient night elven and earthen ancestors appear throughout the continents to share their wisdom and blessings. Elder Darkcore resides in the shadowed halls of the Undercity, bearing witness to the modern realm while offering remembrance to those who seek out the roots of the world.

Approaching Elder Darkcore satisfies an ancient custom of showing respect to the venerable dead and the timeless wardens of Azeroth. In recognition of this pilgrimage, the spirit gifts travelers a Coin of Ancestry as a token of goodwill and enduring memory.
What is the purpose of visiting Elder Darkcore?
Visiting Elder Darkcore during the Lunar Festival allows adventurers to pay homage to the ancient peoples of Azeroth. Speaking with him completes the quest and earns a Coin of Ancestry.

Where can Elder Darkcore be found?
Elder Darkcore manifests in the ruined throne room of Lordaeron, above the Forsaken capital of the Undercity.

The Lunar Festival is an annual season of remembrance and renewal observed across Azeroth, celebrating the triumph over the Burning Legion and paying reverence to ancient elders who guided mortal races.

Elders are ancient spirits, typically linked to the night elves or early earthen cultures, who emerge during the Lunar Festival to bless those who remember their deeds and carry forward the lessons of antiquity.

Elder Darkcore will greet any traveler who manages to reach him, though Alliance players must brave the heavily defended Forsaken capital to do so.

Elder Darkcore allows members of the Horde to partake in the continent-wide rites of the Lunar Festival directly within the safety of an allied capital.
For the Forsaken walking through the ruins of their former kingdom, Elder Darkcore offers an eerie reminder of older times before the Scourge and the fall of Lordaeron.

Elder Stormbrow is one of the ancient spirits honored during the Lunar Festival, standing by the water near Goldshire. Travelers who seek out this elder pay homage to the ancient traditions and the olden races of Azeroth. In return for showing respect, the elder bestows a small token of remembrance.

Elder Stormbrow manifests near the tranquil pond tucked just behind the smithy in Goldshire. While the town usually bustles with armored guards, tradesfolk, and weary adventurers heading into the forest, the arrival of this honored spirit brings a quiet pause. Standing beneath the peaceful canopy of Elwynn Forest, Stormbrow welcomes anyone willing to honor the long history of the realm.

The Lunar Festival marks a time when the spirits of great ancestors return to walk among the living. Elder Stormbrow commends mortal travelers for taking the time to remember those who came before. In exchange for acknowledging the wisdom and legacy of the elder peoples, he grants his blessing and a commemorative coin to celebrate the season.
Where can I find Elder Stormbrow?
Elder Stormbrow stands right by the pond situated directly behind the blacksmith's forge in Goldshire, within Elwynn Forest.

Elder Stormbrow is an ancestral spirit who appears during the Lunar Festival, representing the revered elders of the olden races of Azeroth.

What is the purpose of visiting Elder Stormbrow?
Visiting Elder Stormbrow allows travelers to pay respects to the ancient ancestors during the festival. In return for honoring these traditions, he offers his greetings and a token of appreciation.
why visit stormbrow | elder stormbrow quest | stormbrow the elder purpose
Can Horde players speak to Elder Stormbrow?
While the Lunar Festival elders honor all who seek them out in peace, Goldshire is heavily guarded Alliance territory, making any visit by Horde travelers exceedingly perilous.

Elder Stormbrow offers a Coin of Ancestry, a traditional token of respect and remembrance shared by elders throughout the festival.

Resting right in the heart of Elwynn Forest, Elder Stormbrow is one of the most accessible ancestral spirits for young Alliance adventurers passing through Goldshire.
For humans living in Elwynn, the presence of Elder Stormbrow serves as a reminder of ancient history beyond the walls and recent wars of Stormwind.

Mebok Mizzyrix, an enterprising goblin in Ratchet, believes the cunning of local raptors is stored entirely in their horns. He hires travelers to hunt Sunscale Scytheclaws across the Barrens to collect intact horns for a bizarre commercial venture.

Ratchet is full of goblins seeking their next fortune, and Mebok Mizzyrix is no exception. Observing that the raptors of the Barrens display unusual craftiness and coordination compared to beasts in other regions, Mebok arrived at an eccentric conclusion: their intelligence must be concentrated within their horns. Naturally, rather than conducting formal scientific inquiry, his immediate instinct was to exploit this theoretical resource for profit.

To test his theory, Mebok needs pristine specimens from Sunscale Scytheclaws, some of the deadliest predators in the region. These raptors prowl both the southern stretches of the Barrens and the northern borders approaching Ashenvale. Slaying them and extracting their horns undamaged requires considerable martial skill, as the beasts hunt in packs and defend their territory fiercely.

Once secured, Mebok's plan is simple and characteristically crude: grind the intact horns down into fine powder and brew them into consumable concoctions. Dubbing the resulting mixture 'smart drinks,' he envisions selling the draft to patrons eager to purchase wit in a bottle, fully convinced it will make him wealthy overnight.
Why does Mebok Mizzyrix want raptor horns?
Mebok believes that the exceptional intelligence shown by Barrens raptors is stored in their horns. He intends to grind them into a powder to brew 'smart drinks' and sell them for a handsome profit.
why raptor horns | mebok goal | what does mebok want
Sunscale Scytheclaws roam two distinct parts of the Barrens: the southern regions and the northern plains up near the border of Ashenvale Forest.

While Barrens raptors are known for their cunning, Mebok's belief that their brains or wit reside in their cranial horns is goblin pseudoscience driven purely by profit rather than natural history.

Yes. Ratchet is an open port managed by the Steamwheedle Cartel, and Mebok is a neutral goblin who gladly does business with both the Horde and the Alliance.

Hunters familiar with the raptor packs of Kalimdor understand their deadly cunning well, though Mebok's belief that their wit can be bottled is pure goblin quackery.
Ratchet offers Alliance adventurers a rare neutral foothold in the Horde-dominated Barrens, giving them a chance to earn coin and Steamwheedle favor through odd jobs like Mebok's.

Graveborn the Elder is a Lunar Festival encounter situated near the town of Brill in Tirisfal Glades. During the celebration, travelers seek out Elder Graveborn among the blighted groves to honor the ancient forebears of Azeroth. Paying respects to this spirit earns his blessing and a token of the holiday.

While the Forsaken dwell among ruined manors and grave sites in Tirisfal Glades, the Lunar Festival brings an unexpected communion with ancient times. Elder Graveborn appears as a spectral elder stationed just outside Brill. Even in a realm shattered by the Scourge and reclaimed by the undead, he welcomes pilgrims who pause to honor the ancient ways.

The Lunar Festival marks a time when the great spirits of long-past eras return to offer wisdom and gratitude. When travelers approach Elder Graveborn, he remarks on how heartening it is that the inhabitants of Tirisfal still offer homage to the ancestors despite the land's current decay, bestowing a Coin of Ancestry upon those who greet him.
Elder Graveborn is found near the settlement of Brill in Tirisfal Glades, standing quietly near the roadside outside the town.
elder graveborn location | where is graveborn | graveborn coords
What happens when you speak to Elder Graveborn?
Upon greeting him, Elder Graveborn commends you for honoring the ancient peoples of Azeroth and awards a Coin of Ancestry as part of the Lunar Festival celebrations.
graveborn reward | lunar festival graveborn | what does he give you
Why is an ancient elder standing in Tirisfal Glades?

During the Lunar Festival, the spirits of ancient ancestors manifest across all of Azeroth, from the kaldorei forests to lands torn by war and plague. Elder Graveborn watches over the northern reaches of Lordaeron to ensure its history is not entirely eclipsed by death.
why is he in tirisfal | graveborn lore | who is elder graveborn
Can Alliance players visit Elder Graveborn?

Elder Graveborn himself is a neutral spirit of wisdom and will speak with members of both the Alliance and the Horde. However, because he is right outside the Forsaken town of Brill, Alliance adventurers must beware the local guards.

What is the Coin of Ancestry used for?
Coins of Ancestry gathered from elders like Graveborn can be traded in Moonglade during the Lunar Festival for festive garments, firework recipes, and other celebratory tokens.

Is Elder Graveborn one of the Forsaken?

No. Despite his name and ghostly visage near Brill, Elder Graveborn is one of the ancient spirits celebrated during the Lunar Festival, belonging to the long lineage of Azeroth's elders rather than Sylvanas's Forsaken.

brill | coin of ancestry | elder graveborn | graveborn | lunar festival | tirisfal glades
Druids reverence the Lunar Festival elders as links to the ancient world before the Sundering, heedless of the troubled faction boundaries they inhabit.
Alliance adventurers seeking out Elder Graveborn must tread carefully through Tirisfal Glades, as Brill is a heavily fortified Forsaken haven.
For the Forsaken living in Brill, the arrival of ancient ancestral spirits provides a stark reminder of Azeroth's deeper history beyond the recent tragedies of the Scourge.

Goldwell the Elder is a Lunar Festival quest offered by Elder Goldwell in Kharanos, Dun Morogh. Honoring him reflects the enduring tradition of seeking out ancestral spirits across the snowbound dwarven lands. In exchange for your respects, he bestows a token of ancestral blessing.

Standing in the bitter cold beside the Thunderbrew Distillery in Kharanos, Elder Goldwell watches over the bustling trade path leading to the gates of Ironforge. During the Lunar Festival, this venerable figure welcomes weary travelers, adventurers, and locals alike, embodying the long memory of ancient days when early mortals walked beneath the stars of Azeroth.

Approaching Goldwell offers a moment of reflection amidst the harsh winter winds of Dun Morogh. He expresses relief and joy that mortals still remember the ancient races and their deeds, thanking all who pause their journeys to show respect. In turn, he awards a sacred Coin of Ancestry as an emblem of his blessing.
Where can I find Elder Goldwell?
Elder Goldwell stands right outside the Thunderbrew Distillery inn in the town of Kharanos, situated along the snowy road of Dun Morogh just southwest of the gates to Ironforge.
elder goldwell location | where is elder goldwell | goldwell spot
What is the purpose of seeking out Elder Goldwell?

Elder Goldwell is visited during the Lunar Festival as part of honoring the world's ancient spirits. Paying him your respects proves that the mortal races have not forgotten the sacrifices and wisdom of antiquity.
why visit elder goldwell | what does elder goldwell do | goldwell quest
What reward does Elder Goldwell provide?
He rewards travelers with a Coin of Ancestry, a blessed token bestowed by the festival elders that can be presented to the Cenarion Circle in Moonglade for celebratory festival goods.

Yes. Festival elders like Goldwell are neutral ancestral spirits who welcome adventurers of any faction, though Horde travelers must tread carefully to avoid the watchful dwarven mountaineers patrolling Kharanos.

The Lunar Festival elders manifest across every corner of Azeroth where mortal civilizations have forged enduring communities. Goldwell chose Kharanos to share his blessings with those dwelling near the dwarven kingdom's heart.

Can you complete this quest more than once?
No. The honor paid to Elder Goldwell is offered once per festival season, granting a single blessing and coin to each adventurer who seeks his counsel.

Nestled in safe Alliance territory, Goldwell is one of the easiest elders for young Alliance heroes journeying between Coldridge Valley and Ironforge to visit.
Reaching Goldwell requires sneaking deep into Dun Morogh, braving dwarven guards and bitter cold just outside the high gates of Ironforge.
For dwarves returning from Ironforge, meeting an elder of ancient lineage right outside their premier tavern in Kharanos bridges timeless reverence with hometown pride.

Harpy Raiders is an early offensive task given by Darsok Swiftdagger at the Crossroads to curb the aggressive Witchwing flock. Tasked with hunting down baseline raiders and roguefeathers in the northwestern Barrens, adventurers harvest talons to cripple the flock's supply raids.

Caravans crawling across the dusty trails of the Barrens face constant harassment from wild beasts and quillboar, but the Witchwing harpies pose a particularly deadly aerial nuisance. Striking from the rocky crags in the northwest, these feral creatures routinely sweep down upon merchant trains and supply wagons, slaughtering pack animals and pillaging critical goods bound for orcish outposts.

Rather than launching a haphazard assault against the mountainous roosts, the orc rogue Darsok Swiftdagger has spent days scouting the flock's habits and hierarchy. He knows that an uncoordinated strike will scatter them into the winds. To decisively break the Witchwing, Darsok intends to systematically butcher the flock from the bottom rank up, beginning with the front-line raiders before moving against their commanders.
Why is the Horde targeting the Witchwing harpies?
The Witchwing flock nests in the northwestern crags of the Barrens and regularly swoops down to raid Horde supply caravans traveling along the main trails.

Darsok is an orc scout and rogue stationed at the Crossroads. He monitors local threats and has scoped out the chain of command within the local harpy flock to organize a calculated extermination effort.
darsok | darsok swiftdagger lore | who is darsok
Why does Darsok want Witchwing talons?
Darsok demands the severed talons as concrete proof of the kill, collecting them as grim trophies and confirmation that the flock's lowest raiding ranks are shrinking.
They make their roosts among the thorn-choked bluffs and ravines in the far northwestern stretches of the Barrens, north of the road to Stonetalon.

Darsok Swiftdagger's strategy appeals directly to assassins: scout the target, dissect the hierarchy, and eliminate leadership piece by piece.
Securing the interior pathways through the Barrens is essential to keeping the newly established outposts supplied and unified under Orgrimmar's banners.

Runetotem the Elder is an encounter with an ancestral spirit during the Lunar Festival in Durotar. Found standing within Razor Hill under a pillar of heavenly light, she offers blessings and festival tokens to travelers who come to pay their respects to the past.

During the Lunar Festival, the spirits of ancient elders materialize across Azeroth to commune with the living. Elder Runetotem manifests inside Razor Hill, positioned just past the southern entrance. Bathed in a clear beam of starlight from above, she watches over the orcish settlement and welcomes adventurers who step aside from their travels to acknowledge the wisdom of those who came before.

Approaching Elder Runetotem does more than honor an individual ancestor. In exchange for your homage, she rewards you with a festival token of fortune and shares word of where other spirits may be found, pointing wanderers toward Elder Darkhorn and Elder High Mountain across the continent.
Elder Runetotem is located inside Razor Hill in Durotar, positioned just to the right immediately after entering through the southern entrance.

Honoring Elder Runetotem rewards a festival token commemorating your respect for the ancestors, and she offers directions toward other wandering spirits like Elder Darkhorn and Elder High Mountain.

Standing right inside the walls of Razor Hill, Elder Runetotem is one of the safest and most convenient ancestors for young Horde travelers to honor early in their journeys.
Meeting a spirit bearing the revered Runetotem family name outside the plains of Mulgore serves as a potent reminder of your people's deep spiritual heritage across Kalimdor.

Bloodhoof the Elder is an encounter with one of the venerated ancestral spirits who manifests during the Lunar Festival. Located just outside Bloodhoof Village in Mulgore, this honored spirit acknowledges the respect paid by wandering travelers and grants an ancestral token in return.

During the celebration of the Lunar Festival, the spirits of great heroes and elders from ages past return to Azeroth. Shrouded in celestial radiance, Elder Bloodhoof appears just north of Bloodhoof Village near the bridge. Approaching these venerated ancestors is an act of honoring past sacrifices, and in exchange, Elder Bloodhoof offers words of encouragement and a sacred Coin of Ancestry.

Standing on the ancestral lands of Mulgore, Elder Bloodhoof serves as a bridge between the living tauren tribes and the memory of their forebears. For the tauren, honoring the dead is a pillar of spiritual life, reinforcing the harmony between the Earth Mother, the ancestors, and those currently walking the plains.
Where can I find Elder Bloodhoof?

Travelers seek out Elder Bloodhoof during the Lunar Festival to pay their respects to the ancestors. In recognition of this honor, the spirit rewards visitors with a Coin of Ancestry and wisdom about neighboring spirits, such as Elder Wheathoof.

Druids hold the spirits of the Lunar Festival in high regard, communing with the elders to strengthen their natural bond with the earth and stars.
For a shaman, conversing with manifest ancestors like Elder Bloodhoof directly reinforces the living communion between the mortal realm and ancestral spirits.
Reaching Elder Bloodhoof requires slipping into the heart of Mulgore, making this a bold journey through hostile Horde plains.
Greeting Elder Bloodhoof is a sacred duty on home soil, honoring the legacy of the tribe that helped lead the tauren to their peaceful haven in Mulgore.

Elder Skychaser is an ancestral spirit who manifests during the Lunar Festival atop the Sentinel Tower in Westfall. Honoring her allows travelers across the dust-swept plains to pay homage to the wisdom of ages past. In return, the elder acknowledges the burning vigor of the living and grants her blessing.

Amid the troubled scrublands of Westfall, Sentinel Hill stands as the lone fortified redoubt against Defias raiders and roving scavengers. During the Lunar Festival, an ancestral spirit named Elder Skychaser takes her place on the open platform atop the Sentinel Tower. High above the dust and wind, she keeps a patient vigil over the weary soldiers and beleaguered settlers below, welcoming anyone who makes the climb to show respect.

The Lunar Festival marks a sacred season observed across Azeroth, celebrating wisdom, heritage, and the deeds of ancient spirits who walked the earth before the present struggles. When approached, Elder Skychaser recognizes the vital spark within the traveler, accepting their homage and bestowing a token of her favor as a gift of kinship between the living and the honored dead.
Where can I find Elder Skychaser?
Elder Skychaser is located at the very top of Sentinel Tower at Sentinel Hill in Westfall. Climb the spiral stairs within the tower out onto the upper lookout ramparts.

Why is Elder Skychaser standing on top of Sentinel Tower?

Ancestral spirits choose prominent and symbolic locations across Azeroth during the Lunar Festival. The heights of Sentinel Tower provide a watchful vantage over the Westfall basin, allowing the elder to witness travelers braving the frontier.
why is he in sentinel tower | skychaser tower

Druids hold the Lunar Festival sacred, recognizing ancestral manifestations like Skychaser as an enduring link to ancient traditions and deep natural reverence.
Elder Skychaser is conveniently stationed within the heart of the People's Militia base at Sentinel Hill, making her an easy elder to honor while questing through Westfall.
Reaching Elder Skychaser requires stealth, speed, or brute force, as Sentinel Hill is filled with hostile Alliance guards and militia scouts.

Darkhorn the Elder is a seasonal quest completed by seeking out Elder Darkhorn in Orgrimmar during the Lunar Festival. Travelers pay their respects to the honored ancestor, receiving a token of wisdom and celebration in return. She stands in the heart of the Horde capital as a testament to age, survival, and ancestral pride.

During the Lunar Festival, the spirits of revered ancestors manifest across Azeroth to share their wisdom with the living. Elder Darkhorn rests within the fortified ramparts of Orgrimmar, observing the bustle of the young warrior city. Approaching her offers champions of the Horde—and any Alliance adventurer brave enough to slip through the gates—a chance to pay formal homage to those who walked the earth generations before.

Upon receiving greeting and reverence from passing travelers, Elder Darkhorn acknowledges the vibrant spark of life within them. In exchange for honoring the ways of old, she grants a Coin of Ancestry and her personal blessing. These tokens celebrate the triumph over ancient perils and remind the living to cherish the strength passed down through unbroken bloodlines.

For Horde champions, visiting Elder Darkhorn is a convenient opportunity to honor ancestral tradition right within the safety and bustling heart of their capital.

Wheathoof the Elder is an ancestral tauren spirit honored during the Lunar Festival atop the heights of Thunder Bluff. Visiting him is an act of deep reverence, acknowledging the wisdom of the ancestors who watch over Mulgore and the Horde.

Perched high on the windblown mesas of Thunder Bluff, Wheathoof the Elder manifests as an ancestral presence during the Lunar Festival. Tauren culture holds the voices of their ancestors in the highest regard, believing that the spirits of ancient leaders and sages linger to offer guidance and strength to the living.

Travelers who climb the heights to pay their respects to Elder Wheathoof are greeted not as strangers, but as vital flames of life. In exchange for the traveler's homage, the elder bestows a Coin of Ancestry, symbolizing communion between the enduring past and the living champions fighting for the world's future.
He is an honored tauren ancestral spirit manifested atop the city of Thunder Bluff during the Lunar Festival to receive homage from champions across Azeroth.
